headline: Open Interpreter’s filesystem and shell access create medium-to-high interaction risks; python-cheatsheet is read-only and documentation-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the filesystem, use the clipboard, and execute shell commands, so malicious content it ingests could be treated as instructions. python-cheatsheet is read-only documentation, but if its text is copied into Open Interpreter or placed in a shared file, the pathway exists. The shared filesystem bridge makes this plausible by default.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet content is copied into Open Interpreter prompts or files
IF Open Interpreter is run with auto_run enabled
IF both agents share a writable filesystem path
mitigations: Disable auto_run in Open Interpreter
Keep python-cheatsheet content out of shared files
Use separate per-agent directories
Review copied text before pasting into Open Interpreter
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine and has broad network egress, so sensitive local data can flow out if it is prompted to summarize or act on files. python-cheatsheet itself handles no data, but if it is used as a source document in the same workspace, Open Interpreter can expose local contents through its outputs or API calls. The shared filesystem is the main bridge.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present on the host
IF Open Interpreter is asked to inspect or transmit local file contents
IF the two agents share a workspace or clipboard
mitigations: Run Open Interpreter in a separate user account
Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Disable network egress where possible
Use a throwaway directory for python-cheatsheet copies
requires-engineering: sandbox Open Interpreter in Docker

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has broad filesystem write and git modification capability, while python-cheatsheet has no write, network, or subprocess capabilities. There is little direct write-write overlap, so conflict is limited unless an operator manually points both at the same mutable directory. The pair is mostly asymmetric, reducing contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to modify files that python-cheatsheet also serves
IF the operator expects concurrent edits
mitigations: Do not co-edit the same repo
Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches for isolation
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not act on Open Interpreter outputs, so there is no default downstream automation chain. Open Interpreter can generate or execute actions, but the second agent is not an action-taking consumer. Any cascade requires manual copying of outputs, which keeps the blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Open Interpreter output into python-cheatsheet-derived content
IF the output is treated as authoritative without review
IF downstream automation is added outside the profiles
mitigations: Manually verify any copied output
Keep python-cheatsheet as reference only
Do not automate commits from Open Interpreter output
Use a review step before acting on generated text
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any action-taking tool

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter can access the entire local filesystem and use model-provider APIs, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and handles no regulated data. The main compliance issue is local-data exposure if sensitive files are present, but there is no documented residency or retention mismatch between the pair. The other agent is not a compliance driver here.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored on the host
IF Open Interpreter is used to process that regulated data
IF model-provider logging/retention is not separately controlled
mitigations: Exclude regulated files from the workspace
Use a local-only model provider
Review provider retention settings
Run in a separate account or VM
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
